## Repeated-field encoder

The complete function at `0x00490690...0x00490879` is 490 bytes with stock
SHA-256
`7b88e6eb06989ea15f53609cfb030edd26d2cea87440caec2af61c2e6dc53f20`.
An exhaustive halfword-aligned Thumb branch scan finds its sole official
caller at `0x00490BB8` in the regular field encoder.

The encoder reads a 16-bit element count through field auxiliary pointer
`+0x20`; zero count succeeds without output. Except for pointer storage
`type & 0xC0 == 0x80`, a count exceeding the 16-bit maximum at `+0x14`
preserves an existing output error or installs `0x00779FAC`
(`"array max size exceeded"`) and returns zero.

Low-nibble kinds zero through five use packed encoding. The source-owned
field-key writer first emits wire type two. Kinds four and five derive packed
size as count times four or eight. Kinds zero through three run the
source-owned integer adapter over a zeroed size-only output object, advancing
the descriptor data pointer by element size `+0x12` after each success and
restoring the original pointer after a complete sizing pass. Sizing failure
keeps partial pointer progress and propagates the sizing error, falling back
to the pinned word `0x0078DE7C` from `0x004910B8` when none exists. After
emitting the packed-size prefix, a size-only destination appends that many
null bytes logically. A real destination encodes every fixed or integer
element and retains normal partial data-pointer progress on failure.

Kinds six and above encode each element unpacked through the source-owned
value dispatcher. Pointer-backed kinds six and seven temporarily replace the
descriptor data pointer with the current pointed-to element. A null element
emits the descriptor key plus a zero length prefix; a nonnull element uses
the value dispatcher. The original array cursor is restored before its
element-size advance, and only the low byte of this special-path result
controls continuation. Other unpacked results use their full value.

`format_repeated.c` has source SHA-256
`ca9f445a34b9dc03366e06d7389897befa0064c66767fe5fef08b5a9db2673c9`.
`open_cfw_format_repeated_field_encode` compiles to 398 bytes at
`0x007998A4...0x00799A31`. Its ten placement relocations target the
source-owned field-key, value, descriptor-key, prefix, integer, fixed, and
append functions. The regular encoder now links directly to this source
function.

Host execution checks zero count, maximum-count error installation and
preservation, pointer-storage bound bypass, packed four/eight-byte sizing,
key/prefix failures, size-only append, fixed and integer partial progress,
integer sizing restoration and error/fallback propagation, unpacked full-
result behavior, pointer-backed null and nonnull bytes/string elements, and
low-byte failure truncation. Target tests hash-pin the complete stock span,
sole caller, both error words, complete source relocation topology, and the
installed non-linking redirect.

## Protobuf-style default-value checker

The complete recursive function at `0x0049087A...0x00490A45` is 460 bytes
with stock SHA-256
`f70e1069fa8cbdd155d3d1b29e1b50f1c3b75c7c69174ac12d89a7295d410837`.
An exhaustive halfword-aligned Thumb branch scan finds its self-call at
`0x004909B0` and its sole external official caller at `0x00490B64` in the
regular field encoder.

The checker partitions field byte `+0x16` into storage bits `0xC0`,
allocation bits `0x30`, and a low-nibble kind. For static storage, allocation
zero is never considered a default. Repeated and oneof allocations `0x20`
and `0x30` are default when the 16-bit value through auxiliary pointer
`+0x20` is zero. Optional allocation `0x10` with an auxiliary pointer is
default when the source-owned boolean reader reports false. Without that
pointer, a nonzero metadata word at metadata offset `+0x08` prevents default
classification.

For the remaining static optional values, kinds zero through five scan the
`+0x12`-byte data object at `+0x1C` and require every byte to be zero. Kind
six reads a zero 16-bit value; kind seven reads a zero first byte; and kind
11 uses a zero `+0x12` length. Kinds eight and nine initialize a 40-byte
iterator through reviewed Thumb entry `0x004D9385`, passing the
subdescriptor at `+0x24` and data pointer. An empty iterator is default;
otherwise every iterated child must recursively be default, advancing with
reviewed entry `0x004D93D9`. Other kinds are not default.

Pointer storage `0x80` is default only when the data pointer is null. Indirect
storage `0x40`, kind 10, dereferences the data word and tests it for zero.
Other indirect kinds read the metadata callback at `+0x0C`: the special
callback value `0x004D94E7`, pinned by the word at `0x004910BC`, also tests
the data word; any other field is default only when the callback itself is
null. Storage `0xC0` is not default.

`format_default.c` has source SHA-256
`e3338516fe31f21b41799d01271941ec015146e30b9128f4cbab9b8bf422d9c8`.
`open_cfw_format_default_check` compiles to 280 bytes at
`0x0079978C...0x007998A3`. Its two placement relocations call the
source-owned boolean reader and itself recursively; Clang materializes both
reviewed iterator entries directly.

Host execution checks every allocation and storage family, explicit boolean
presence, metadata suppression, all scalar zero scans, bytes/string/span
defaults, invalid kinds, empty/all-default/nondefault recursive submessages,
iterator arguments and call counts, pointer storage, special-callback data
words, null callbacks, and storage `0xC0`. Target tests hash-pin the complete
stock span, both raw callers, special-callback literal, source-call topology,
fixed iterator entries, and installed non-linking redirect.

16-bit length, one downstream call, and unchanged result propagation. The
wider formatter remains a version-pinned source/blob ABI.

## Shared microsecond delay primitive

The common duration primitive is the complete 92-byte function and literal
span at `0x004807A0...0x004807FB`. Its stock SHA-256 is
`10ca20e1a01a30d82ec2e215caaa2abe57087c1e68ff4182e4e848d974326a6f`;
the first 80 code bytes independently hash to
`f95193c502160b469e1579e13223f1cdf488a2d8fab9ec07f686c9101fbed753`.
A raw-image Thumb scan finds 116 direct `BL` callers. Keeping the replacement
at its original address preserves every one of those callers without
redirect stubs.

The recovered body:

1. converts the unsigned microsecond argument to float and then to fixed point
   with five fractional bits, producing the initial `usec * 32` cycle-loop
   iteration count;
2. reads Apollo510 `PWRCTRL.MCUPERFREQ` at `0x40021000` and extracts status
   bits 3 through 4;
3. for status two, rescales the count by `250 / 96` and uses calibrated
   adjustment 24;
4. for every other status, leaves the 96 MHz-derived count unchanged and uses
   calibrated adjustment 15; and
5. only subtracts the adjustment and calls the lower cycle loop when the count
   is strictly greater than the adjustment.

The internal call instruction at `0x004807EA` resolves to `0x00000040`.
Ambiq's Apollo510 SDK source identifies this as `br_util_delay_cycles`, a
three-cycle `SUBS`/`BNE` loop in ITCM, rather than a Boot ROM service. The
official application tail at load-image storage
`0x00794310...0x00794315` contains the matching bytes
`01 38 FD D1 70 47`; their SHA-256 is
`c5c855e6f7cfc08b58f586a46b44b895bc33bda66242061d73357d9f93e76471`.
Apollo510's public register map defines ITCM as
`0x00000000...0x0003FFFF`, which includes the recovered runtime address.

The runtime mapping is recovered from reset, rather than inferred from the
matching bytes. Vector entry one points to reset at `0x005E4232`. Reset calls
startup at `0x005E4294`; startup first sets VTOR to `0x00438000` through
`0x005E4228`, then calls the scatter loader at `0x005E42B4`. That loader walks
records at `0x0075D3C8...0x0075D40F`. Its second record at `0x0075D3E0`
contains:

- relative handler `0xFFCDCD3F`, resolving to Thumb decompressor
  `0x0043A11E`;
- relative source `0x00036F2A`, resolving to `0x0079430E`;
- encoded size `0x2C`, representing a 22-byte compressed stream; and
- absolute destination `0x00000040`.

The stream is
`10 0B 01 38 FD D1 70 47 70 47 50 F8 04 3B 41 04 30 01 01 3A F9 10`.
Its first token `0x10` and literal extension `0x0B` emit the following 14
bytes literally. Consequently storage `0x00794310...0x00794315` maps exactly
to ITCM `0x00000040...0x00000045`; the neighboring literal and compressed
bytes describe other ITCM functions and are not part of this replacement.

`duration_delay.c` is a bounded BSD-3-Clause adaptation of AmbiqSuite SDK
5.1.0
[`am_hal_utils.c`](https://github.com/AmbiqMicro/ambiqhal_ambiq/blob/e8baebd44008dfec7197d40d53c8a62f3a36b38b/mcu/apollo510/hal/mcu/am_hal_utils.c)
at commit `e8baebd44008dfec7197d40d53c8a62f3a36b38b`; the corresponding
[`am_reg_base_addresses.h`](https://github.com/AmbiqMicro/ambiqhal_ambiq/blob/e8baebd44008dfec7197d40d53c8a62f3a36b38b/mcu/apollo510/regs/am_reg_base_addresses.h)
supplies the ITCM boundary. The target definition uses explicit source
assembly so calibrated instruction scheduling, PC-relative literals, and the
placement-dependent ITCM `BL` remain exact. `open_cfw_delay_us` compiles to a
92-byte builder input at `0x007990C8...0x00799123`; the component builder's exact-copy
patch validates both compiled size and the pinned stock span before copying
those bytes back to `0x004807A0`. `open_cfw_delay_cycles` independently
compiles to the exact six bytes at overlay `0x007990C0...0x007990C5`; a second
exact-copy patch installs them at load-image storage `0x00794310`.

The adjacent application wrappers are source-owned as exact copies too:

- `0x004910F4...0x00491101`, 14 bytes, SHA-256
  `566ba14b421d07c4b79a1aba6d3cf0e75b0ce4ad752150e6690288bddf79f59f`,
  multiplies the unsigned argument by 1,000 and calls `0x004807A0`; a direct
  Thumb scan finds 53 callers.
- `0x00491102...0x00491109`, 8 bytes, SHA-256
  `5d53c0f861f1e995a334442c81f3f3f1f5df6dac4f8685c61ffadf12303c79fc`,
  passes the unsigned microsecond argument unchanged; a direct Thumb scan
  finds 66 callers.

Their builder-input functions compile at `0x00799124...0x00799131` and
`0x00799134...0x0079913B`; exact-copy patches install them at their original
addresses, where their placement-specific branches resolve to the
source-owned in-place delay.

The compiled in-place bytes are byte-identical to stock. Operation zero,
operation one, and IRQ bit-6 cleanup now call fixed Thumb entry `0x004807A1`.
This is deliberate: the exact-copy builder input contains a raw ITCM branch
encoded for `0x004807EA` and must never execute from its overlay staging
address. Target tests prove the three consumers materialize `0x004807A1` and
that no linker relocation targets the staging symbol. Host substitution executes
the same policy with controlled performance status and cycle-loop hooks.
Tests cover zero duration, one and 1,000 microseconds at LP and HP, statuses
zero and three following the LP path, a large-duration case, exact call
suppression at/below adjustment, exact calculated loop iterations, one
millisecond through the scaling wrapper, and one microsecond through the
passthrough wrapper. The
component builder additionally fails closed unless the scatter record resolves
the configured handler, stream, destination, first literal run, and
storage-to-runtime mapping. A negative fixture changes the destination to
`0x00000044` and proves that drift is rejected before patching. The six-byte
ITCM function and its load-image literal are therefore source-owned; the
scatter loader, record table, stream framing, and adjacent compressed ITCM
functions remain official compatibility dependencies.

The function reads CHIPPN, CHIPID0, CHIPID1, CHIPREV, VENDORID, and SKU from
`0x40020000...0x40020014`, writes qualified value one, and deliberately leaves
the 32-bit flash-size field at output offset 28 untouched. It performs fresh
SKU reads for MRAM, ITCM, DTCM, and shared-SRAM indexing. The reviewed stock

JEDEC PID0...PID3 at `0xE00FEFE0...0xE00FEFEC` produce the part number,

## Apollo510 public MCUCTRL control dispatcher at `0x004809C4`

The public Apollo510 `am_hal_mcuctrl_control` function is the complete
658-byte stock span `0x004809C4...0x00480C55`, with SHA-256
`eb3d3bb0a11febea901aa2630257bf91b9993e4b363b608e875ac34871df3624`.

Exhaustive halfword-aligned branch decoding finds no raw `B.W` entry caller,
no external branch into the function interior, and no aligned stored Thumb
pointer to its entry or interior.

The function dispatches on the low byte of its command and implements all
seven public operations numbered zero through six: 32 kHz crystal enable and
disable, 32 MHz crystal kick-start, normal operation, disable, clock-output
enable, and clock-output disable. The source preserves the exact volatile
read/modify/write order for `XTALCTRL` at `0x40020120`, `XTALHSTRIMS` at
`0x40020128`, and `XTALHSCTRL` at `0x4002012C`, plus the cap-trim values at
`0x200001E0` and `0x200001E4`. It preserves three especially non-obvious
stock rules:

- command 5 requests clock 2 for user `0x34` before validating arguments;
- a valid non-null command-5 argument is read twice, and only zero or values
  three through seven are accepted;
- command 6 changes both oscillator registers before releasing the clock and
  returns a release failure after those writes.

The only three executable dependencies are delay entry `0x004807A0`,
clock-request entry `0x004C44BC`, and clock-release entry `0x004C4530`, called
at stock sites `0x00480AA2`, `0x00480BC6`, and `0x00480C46`. The source uses
their reviewed Thumb entries `0x004807A1`, `0x004C44BD`, and `0x004C4531`.

SHA-256 values
`3a75caa326f613bf3aaeba99b1354a9824249b2ed6d139ba2b72010e8eba9500`
and
`6504a1af04209e0c111e704a63f0628537a0c59ed8750806784e049fc21fc7f8`.

## Apollo510 MCUCTRL trim-version decoder at `0x00480C7C`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the private `trim_version_get` helper as the complete
246-byte stock span `0x00480C7C...0x00480D71`, with SHA-256
`4e7c5d4c775be7a1a4cc04083e48387e4afbee82847afee4566ed22133804179`.
Its sole executable caller is the FEATURES_AVAIL branch at `0x00480E58` in
the public `am_hal_mcuctrl_info_get` function beginning at `0x00480D72`.
Exhaustive halfword-aligned branch decoding finds no raw `B.W` entry caller
or external interior target, and the aligned stored-Thumb-pointer scan finds
neither the entry nor an interior address. The sole executable dependency is
the INFO1 reader call at `0x00480C8A` to `0x004D3F3C`.

The helper calls that reader as `read(1, 0x244, 1, &trim_version)`, clears the
packed trim word at feature-structure offset `+0x0C`, and returns the reader
status unchanged. A successful read performs one, two, or three fresh
volatile `CHIPREV` reads at `0x4002000C` according to short-circuit progress.
Major revision 2, minor revision at least 2, and a trim value below 255 select
PCM 2.x encoding. Minor revision 3 is already zero-based; every other
qualifying minor revision decrements the one-based trim value. The packed
word then contains major 2, the byte-truncated minor value, PCM bit 17, and
valid bit 16. Other successful reads select non-PCM major zero, retain the
byte-truncated minor value, clear PCM, and set valid. Reader failures retain
only the byte-truncated trim value and leave PCM and valid clear.

Eight standalone host tests cover the INFO1 call ABI, returned status,
feature-word offset, B1 decrement, B2 zero-based behavior, PCM qualification
and short-circuit register-read counts, reader failures, 1,000 deterministic
randomized stock models, complete stock/following spans, the CHIPREV literal,
call/dependency topology, and stored-pointer absence. The stock entry receives
a hash-validated non-linking `B.W` and 121 NOP halfwords. The 246-byte
replacement has SHA-256
`90fcd90b7dbaebafde1b1a2def63e895f979d27dc1570d115126dceb9390364b`
and targets `open_cfw_mcuctrl_trim_version_get` at `0x007AB028`. The compiled
function is 96 bytes at overlay offset 93,444, has SHA-256
`cbde6cb01da36cb2866c1218e8484e37cbfe95d967c9fba22090be4b4eccf17a`,
and introduces no linker relocation. The following 250-byte public
information getter is now independently source-owned; only its 108-byte
literal/alignment pool at `0x00480E6C...0x00480ED7` remains opaque, with
SHA-256
`4664f5a57e3b6a2fb5f9ce35b8570c1206f968cfad80379ef25a54da04695483`.

## Shared ASCII case-folding primitive at `0x00481830`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the complete leaf routine at
`0x00481830...0x00481835`, six bytes, with exact bytes
`40f020007047` and SHA-256
`ba0e75482a025061a99348c4060bc9de61f721b82599d840f94f2ac532612778`.
The two instructions are `orr r0,r0,#0x20` and `bx lr`; decompilation recovers
the exact unsigned 32-bit expression `return param_1 | 0x20`. This is an
unconditional bit fold, not a range-checked C-library `tolower`, and it
neither truncates its input nor special-cases nonletters.

Ghidra reports the sole executable caller at `0x0048252C`, inside the
276-byte integer-formatting helper `0x00482518...0x0048262B`. The caller
selects base eight directly for format code `o`; otherwise it folds the
format code and selects base sixteen only when the result is `x`, falling
back to base ten. The complete caller has SHA-256

## Integer-formatting helper at `0x00482518`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the complete helper at
`0x00482518...0x0048262B`, 276 bytes, with SHA-256
`be063cc5e8c7478419a02b8f09e24e93209ee2ec042cdcf325729564f91d4897`.
Its sole indexed executable caller is the call at `0x00482478` inside the
formatting core `0x00481836...0x004824ED`. Immediately before the call, that
caller passes `sp + 8` in `r0` and the full-width conversion specifier from
`r11` in `r1`; immediately afterward it unconditionally branches to
`0x004824AC`. The complete 18-byte caller context
`0x0048246C...0x0048247D` has exact bytes
`12a8079901440591594602a800f04ef816e0` and SHA-256
`961723b60c4644ee76a78ce14bc15a79b953237cc364e1dc0b8e73219c1c8838`.
No result register is consumed.

The stock prologue pushes `r2` and `r3`, and both exits pop those saved words
into `r0` and `r1`. That artifact leads Ghidra to infer an `undefined8`
return, but it is not a semantic result: the sole caller neither initializes
those registers as arguments nor observes them after the call. The recovered
C-level ABI is therefore
`void helper(context, unsigned int specifier)`.

The context fields used by the helper are:

| Offset | Width | Recovered meaning |
|---:|---:|---|
| `+0x00` | 8 | 64-bit input value |
| `+0x0C` | 4 | Current digit/prefix lower-bound pointer |
| `+0x10` | 4 | Base of the 60-byte reverse-digit scratch area |
| `+0x14` | 4 | Existing sign/prefix length |
| `+0x18` | 4 | Generated digit length |
| `+0x20` | 4 | Zero-padding length |
| `+0x30` | 4 | Signed precision; negative means unspecified |
| `+0x34` | 4 | Field width |
| `+0x38` | 2 | Formatting flags |

The source structure also names and preserves the untouched words at
`+0x08`, `+0x1C`, `+0x24`, `+0x28`, and `+0x2C`. Compile-time offset
assertions pin every used field. The recovered flag bits are `0x04` for left
alignment, `0x08` for alternate form, and `0x10` for zero padding.

Specifier `o` selects base eight without calling the fold helper. Every other
specifier is passed full-width to the source-owned unconditional
`value | 0x20` fold; an exact folded result of `x` selects base sixteen, and
all other values select base ten. This intentionally means high bits on the
specifier prevent the octal/hexadecimal comparisons. Only exact full-width
`d` and `i` specifiers treat a value with its high word's sign bit set as a
negative signed input. The helper forms its unsigned two's-complement
magnitude, including the defined `INT64_MIN` magnitude case; sign-prefix
construction belongs to the caller.

Digits are generated backward from scratch offset 60. Each remainder becomes
`remainder + '0'`; values at or above `':'` add the low byte of the original
specifier minus `0x51`, yielding lowercase digits for `x` and uppercase
digits for `X`. After each digit, generation continues only while the
quotient is nonzero and the unsigned 32-bit digit lower-bound pointer is below
the newly written byte. The first digit is always emitted when the normal
path is entered. A zero value with precision zero emits no digit, except that
alternate-form octal emits one `0`. Alternate-form octal otherwise prepends
`0` only when the first generated digit is not already zero.

The helper stores the resulting pointer and `60 - cursor` digit length. When
precision exceeds that length, it replaces the zero-padding count with their
difference and clears flag `0x10` in the complete 16-bit flag field. When
precision is negative and the low flag byte has zero padding without left
alignment, it computes
`width - prefix_length - existing_zero_padding - digit_length` using 32-bit
arithmetic and stores a positive signed result as the new zero-padding count.
All other context fields and unwritten scratch bytes remain unchanged.

The only three stock body dependencies are:

| Call site | Target | Exact bytes | Meaning |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| `0x0048252C` | `0x00481830` | `fff780f9` | Full-width ASCII fold |
| `0x0048258C` | `0x0047CC60` | `faf768fb` | 64-bit unsigned divmod remainder |
| `0x004825A6` | `0x0047CC60` | `faf75bfb` | 64-bit unsigned divmod quotient |

Complete halfword-aligned raw `BL` and `B.W` scans find the sole entry call,
no non-linking entry, and no executable external interior target. Narrow
branch scans find no entry, but do find one instruction-shaped halfword
`0xD784` at `0x0048267C` that would target interior address `0x00482588`.
Ghidra classifies its source in the non-code gap
`0x00482672...0x00482683`, and reports no reference to the target. Byte-wise

`0x00448F6D -> 0x00482620`, `0x0046F32D -> 0x004825B4`, and
`0x004AAADB -> 0x00482620`; none is indexed as a Ghidra reference. They are

The retained prefix `0x00481836...0x00482517` is 3,298 bytes with SHA-256

## Decimal power-scaling helper at `0x0048262C`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the complete adjacent helper at
`0x0048262C...0x00482671`, 70 bytes, with SHA-256
`779f44305918c180ef963bd1c49064f2b2b00b9e1decda3934f8ab0b46c25278`.
Its recovered ABI is
`double helper(double value, int exponent)`: the soft-float entry receives
the double words in `r0`/`r1`, the exponent in `r2`, and returns the double
words in `r0`/`r1`.

Both executable callers are inside the retained formatting core. The call at
`0x00481F90` receives `7 - adjustment` only on the strictly positive branch.
On the complementary branch, the caller negates that value, calls the helper
at `0x00481F9E` with `1.0`, and divides the original value by the returned
power. The reviewed caller contract therefore supplies only non-negative
exponents, including zero on the second path. The complete 50-byte context
`0x00481F7C...0x00481FAD` has SHA-256
`437c36dec2c618ea517ea095e33967dfb162960b96e98b4d06ad809fbfea9197`;
the 22-byte dual-call core has exact bytes
`2046294600f04cfb0be052420020dff8dc1600f045fb`.

The helper initializes a factor to `10.0` and performs exponentiation by
squaring. On every iteration it first multiplies the accumulated value when
the current exponent low bit is set, then unconditionally squares the factor,
then arithmetic-shifts the signed exponent right. Exponent zero is an exact
no-call identity. The two stock body calls are:

| Call site | Target | Exact bytes | Meaning |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| `0x0048264C` | `0x004D4354` | `51f082fe` | Accumulated-value double multiply |
| `0x0048265C` | `0x004D4354` | `51f07afe` | Decimal-factor double square |

The retained 18-byte alignment/literal pool
`0x00482672...0x00482683` has exact bytes
`0000a08601000000f03f84d7974100002440` and SHA-256
`193dc16eaca2246df95bb7dd28baae4255adaac92a75550c82d285373443fe7a`.
It contains the caller's `1.0` high word at `0x00482678` and the helper's
`10.0` high word at `0x00482680`; both use an explicit zero low word. The
following function `0x00482684...0x004826B1` is independently bounded at 46
bytes and has SHA-256
`584f21e8f8b4cc13f7994f623e309f9522edb33e3b5d9fa5036650fb429532dc`.

Complete halfword-aligned raw `BL` and `B.W` scans find exactly the two
callers, both multiplication dependencies, no entry jump, and no executable
external interior target. Narrow unconditional, conditional, `CBZ`, and
`CBNZ` scans find no entry or interior target. A byte-aligned whole-image
stored-Thumb-pointer scan likewise finds no entry or interior value.

edges, 256 deterministic finite cross-product cases, both adjacent
boundaries, both callers, both dependencies, and complete negative topology.

receiving the current output state and one zero-extended source byte.

accepted-byte count. A nonzero result increments the unsigned 32-bit count at

## Runtime lookup-layout predicate at `0x00482708`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the complete leaf predicate at
`0x00482708...0x00482715`, 14 bytes, with exact bytes
`007aff2801d1012000e000207047` and SHA-256
`5f4d8578d1c93ca71614bc46df4d853223c3b8e389efde4fef5231c6cde6f999`.
It reads only byte offset eight of its context and returns one exactly when
that byte is the `0xFF` sentinel. Its three callers at `0x00482720`,
`0x004827B8`, and `0x00482872` use that result to select the static
zero-terminated key/value representation and to reject mutation of that
representation. The predicate has no body dependency.

The immediately preceding zero-fill wrapper at `0x004826FC` deliberately
remains opaque. Its epilogue restores the caller's saved `r7` into `r0` after
the fixed zero-fill call at `0x00482702` to `0x00454746`. Although its three
callers at `0x00482790`, `0x004827AA`, and `0x0048295E` treat it as a
void-style operation, reproducing the observable return-register artifact in
portable C would guess at an ABI that the evidence does not justify.
Retaining these 12 exact bytes is therefore a bounded compatibility choice,
not an unidentified function boundary.

## Dual-layout style-property lookup at `0x00482716`

Ghidra 12.1.2 bounds the complete 104-byte helper at
`0x00482716...0x0048277D`, with SHA-256
`094798629ce86c61f6c7e0aee2be68676cb8e7629dba07c4d0a2959a63dabcce`.
The recovered ABI is
`unsigned lookup(const map *, unsigned key, unsigned *result)`. The map stores
its table pointer at `+0x00`, an otherwise unused property-group bitmap at
`+0x04`, and a count/layout byte at `+0x08`.

Counts zero through 254 select a mutable packed representation: `count`
little-endian 32-bit values followed immediately by `count` one-byte property
keys. The helper normalizes the key argument to its low byte, searches keys in
ascending index order, writes the corresponding value on the first match, and
returns one. Zero count or a miss returns zero without writing the result.
Count `0xFF` selects a static representation of eight-byte records with key at
offset zero and value at offset four. Key zero terminates the static table and
therefore cannot match.

The stock body has one dependency, its call at `0x00482720` to the
source-owned layout predicate at `0x00482708`. Its sole direct caller is the
public adapter call at `0x0048294A`. Complete wide/narrow branch scans find no
entry jump or exterior interior target. A byte-wise word scan finds one
unaligned value at `0x004AAAE5` that decodes to interior address
`0x00482720`; it crosses instruction bytes, lies outside the recognized
topology, and has no indexed Ghidra reference.

Ten standalone tests exercise empty and singleton maps, duplicate
first-match behavior, maximum mutable count, both layouts, zero keys, static
termination, high-word key normalization, miss immutability, wrapper context,
exact stock/adjacent spans, complete topology, and 512 deterministic
randomized cases.

The stock entry receives a hash-validated non-linking `B.W` followed by 50
NOP halfwords. The 104-byte replacement has SHA-256
`302da71ef485ae984b6023d9235e34a41386127da1279affb967f59aec42b517`
and targets `open_cfw_runtime_byte_map_lookup` at `0x007AB344`. The compiled
source body is 118 bytes at overlay offset 94,240, has SHA-256

and has no relocation.

Head and tail insertion deliberately dereference a null list, while
insert-before alone rejects null list and active-node arguments. All three
allocate the wrapped `node_size + 8`, preserve the exact setter and descriptor
publication order, and return zero without mutation on allocation failure.
Insert-before delegates the head case directly to the source-owned head
routine; a malformed null previous pointer retains the stock orphan-node
quirk.

Removal remains an unlink operation, not a free operation. It gives the head
case precedence, updates the descriptor before clearing the surviving
endpoint link, leaves the removed node's links untouched, and performs no
node-null or membership validation. The middle path writes
`previous->next` before `next->previous`, including the stock behavior that
forged nonmember links can rewire unrelated nodes.

Custom clear captures the next pointer before any action. A non-null callback
owns cleanup and receives each node without implicit removal or freeing. A
null callback invokes the source-patched unlink entry and then the retained
allocator free entry. The stock epilogue's leaked scratch value in `r0` is
not a semantic return.

one caller of custom clear. Wide/narrow entry and exterior-interior scans find
no alternate topology. The three unaligned stored-pointer-looking candidates
are pinned as instruction-byte false positives. The only indirect control
transfer in the cluster is the cleanup callback's `BLX r6`.

The following `0x00482F72...0x00482F73` alignment bytes are exactly

`96a296d224f285c67bee93c30f8a309157f0daa35dc5b87e410b78630a09cfc7`.

The RGB888 helper uses three-byte aggregate values in B/G/R order in `r0`
and `r1`, truncates opacity in `r2` to its low byte, and computes every lane
as `floor((c1 * opacity + c2 * (255 - opacity)) / 255)`. The stock fourth
return byte is unwritten aggregate padding and has no semantic value. Its 14
direct callers are `0x0044CBEA`, `0x00452E5E`, and
`0x005C909C...0x005C92C6`; their ordered-address digest is
`205d15dd4ad3ca2cef7d248205eab58ff56352467de5db4a2b4472ad263320ab`.

Packed words place blue, green, red, and alpha in ascending bytes. The
packed mixer returns the destination unchanged for source alpha below three,
copies source RGB while retaining destination alpha above 252, and otherwise
uses three intentionally darkening divide-by-256 lane computations. Its only
stock callers are the two instruction-aligned calls at `0x00482F28` and
`0x00482F64`; their address digest is
`3a105ffba24f640a8a40295d35f547f35d428282c5fcf602a269b5bbcb3100af`.
The brightness helper returns `(4 * blue + green + 3 * red) >> 3`; its six
direct callers have digest
`f099e95e0fad06fb9d143e1ab71861ee19989da26741c1b027bb50453e51b6c0`.

The two-layer composer gives fully opaque foreground and nearly transparent
background precedence, returns background for nearly transparent
foreground, delegates directly to the packed mixer for opaque background,
and otherwise computes
`255 - (((255 - foreground_alpha) * (255 - background_alpha)) >> 8)`.
It converts foreground alpha to `(foreground_alpha * 255) / result_alpha`
for the mix and restores the composite alpha afterward. Its two direct
callers at `0x0044C578` and `0x00452EAC` have ordered-address digest
`b3f1d517474c23b2d5301a8bf62074ae181bc975d7ca9d323f7cab24156b8aa5`.
The production dependency uses the source-patched Thumb entry
`0x00482E4D`; combined compilation independently resolves both internal
calls to `open_cfw_runtime_color_mix_alpha`.

Whole-image instruction-aligned BL/B.W, exterior-interior branch, and
byte-wise stored-pointer scans find no alternate entry topology. Apparent
unaligned calls and stored interior values are pinned as overlapping
instruction bytes, not control-flow or data pointers. The behavior also
matches the corresponding operations in the official
[LVGL 9.3 color-operation source](https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/v9.3.0/src/misc/lv_color_op.c).

The integrated overlay emits the four bodies at

The public theme group is a 90-byte contiguous span with SHA-256
`7e0a30860c051b990a19bd02045a981aed535b61e6a500bfdaa932668ca13dbf`.
It selects either the object's display or the default display, forwards that
display to the active-theme getter, removes all object styles before applying
a non-null theme, and returns the three-byte B/G/R primary-color field at
theme offset 16. A null theme falls back to palette index 17. The two
source-internal theme-resolver calls are linked directly. The public-apply
routine is semantically void; stock incidentally returns its saved incoming
`r3`, and both callers ignore that value. The three-byte color return likewise
has a nonsemantic high `r0` padding byte in stock; all four callers store only
the three meaningful bytes.

The two private traversals model only fields observed in stock: theme
`apply_cb` at `+0`, parent at `+4`, object class pointer at `+0`, and class
base and flags at `+0` and `+32`. The chain walks parents first and invokes
each non-null callback with `r0=theme`, `r1=object`, and `r2=callback`.
Class traversal descends only when bit 20 is set, restores the original class
pointer at every level, and produces the base-first class/theme cross product.
The only apparent stored interior values,
`0x005354D7 -> 0x00482FD4` and
`0x004AA08F -> 0x00483020`, are unaligned byte-stream false positives.

The formatting group is a contiguous 68-byte span with SHA-256
`1202ca15ca8a150cea25a8c24c59038567b45a47be5e42564dfe24147cd5176b`.
The store writes the low byte only when its unsigned index is below capacity.
The no-op compiles to the exact stock two-byte `bx lr` and is copied in place
because a four-byte entry redirect cannot fit; its four-argument output
callback signature is inferred from the adjacent paired callback table, while
its complete observable behavior is the verified no-op. The digit predicate
tests only the low byte. The decimal parser advances its byte cursor across
digits and performs modulo-2^32 `10 * value + digit` accumulation.
Stored Thumb entries at `0x00484010` and `0x0048400C` preserve the store and
no-op callbacks. The digit callers at `0x00483060`, `0x00483A14`, and
`0x00483A60` have ordered-address digest
`d05911a4c298614373b6b6cc31befb0b301957967ea31a93060f8726058b78c9`;
the parser callers at `0x00483A1E` and `0x00483A6A` have digest
`d892bc433717618ec3f64b4d804cea0de1add80f028702536c4045c05a1a4416`.

Whole-image instruction-aligned wide and narrow branch, exterior-interior
target, and byte-wise stored-pointer scans find no alternate entry topology.
The recovered theme behavior matches the official
[LVGL 9.3 theme source](https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/v9.3.0/src/themes/lv_theme.c).

The complete 426-byte stock span has SHA-256

Its 28-byte descriptor stores mutex, TLSF control, current bytes, unsigned
peak bytes, arena size, and arena base in six 32-bit words; the policy byte at
`+0x18` belongs to the higher selector and remains untouched.

Initialization creates TLSF first and a normal priority-inheritance mutex
second, emits the exact reviewed diagnostic on either failure, and then spins.
Allocation and aligned allocation bypass size zero, accept only mutex-take
result one, account the usable TLSF block size with unsigned wrap, update the
unsigned peak, and always release an acquired mutex. Reallocation always
locks—even for a null pointer or size zero—measures the old block before the
backend call, and updates accounting only for a non-null result. This
deliberately preserves the stock non-null/size-zero stale-accounting defect.
Free bypasses null, measures before freeing, and saturates current bytes to
zero when the block size is greater than or equal to the current count.

The stable FreeRTOS mutex create/take/give Thumb identities are
`0x004416D7`, `0x00441C45`, and `0x004417EF`. Those public queue entries now
redirect to the source implementation described below, while their reviewed
private queue, task, list, and port dependencies remain retained ABI seams.

`0x004D0723`, `0x004D0745`, `0x004D0809`, and `0x004D0869`, which redirect
to the integrated source allocator. The diagnostic call resolves internally

The only initializer calls are at `0x004842F0`, `0x004842FE`, and

`def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c`. The selected upstream file
has SHA-256
`5cdf4fa35fe059446effff5bf20deaf83ddffb08921bc198fda106b1d17dd894`.
The complete contiguous stock `queue.c` closure is
`0x00441516...0x00442079`, 2,916 bytes, with SHA-256
`04237f42f61134a43524f8cba5e7f50b75ddc5702a2f9801e3c21a0d12ff7948`.
The shared port functions beginning at `0x0044207C` are outside that
closure.

An exhaustive branch and stored-pointer audit finds respectively four,
seven, five, 15, and ten direct `BL` callers of the five replaced entries,
zero `B.W` callers, zero exterior branches into their interiors, and zero
stored entry or interior pointers. The caller-address digests are respectively
`23540d6e3112e00dcde5b88bf3d003e6dc3087cd09dc09532561284102a9cae1`,
`637f30fef353a32d0fe7404c3262cb39f4c4fda6430dbc196928e27de6864e4a`,
`a254f61a532cba1a92f37282cf387d2b06e74c3b175e1475c2cff49afee47d5a`,
`1680c4be07765cb8bb987b51840ff38cca7c0b98e129db6b75e2f14d44c1b7ee`,
and
`f713585a87faff9b034d775b62f3e98cf2cc6f292bd6fa556731a37588effb91`.
The redirect-entry list digest is
`0bacc39551c3f0b5250097d35143c159ad6b77c08c83bf577459f6bfdcc49902`.
The generic-send callers include real message queues as well as mutexes:
timer commands carry three 32-bit words, while CMSIS wrappers reach the
same function for display, BLE, event-loop, semaphore, and memory-pool
traffic. The implementation therefore preserves the full queue operation
rather than specializing the entry as a mutex give.

The recovered `Queue_t` is exactly 80 bytes. Its directly used offsets are
head/mutex marker `+0x00`, mutex holder `+0x08`, recursive count `+0x0C`,
send and receive wait lists `+0x10` and `+0x24`, message count `+0x38`,
length `+0x3C`, item size `+0x40`, receive/transmit locks `+0x44/+0x45`,
static-allocation marker `+0x46`, trace number `+0x48`, and trace type
`+0x4C`. Compile-time target assertions pin every offset and the total
size. The observed configuration enables mutexes, recursive mutexes,
counting semaphores, preemption, timers, trace metadata, and both allocation
modes; queue sets are disabled.

The source preserves all public behavior: create arguments and null result,
current-owner recursive take and give accounting, final recursive give through
the source-owned generic-send path, first recursive take through the patched
public semaphore-take entry, send-to-back/front/overwrite copying,
immediate full failure, timed blocking, queue locking, timeout retry, waiter
removal, preemptive yield, mutex priority disinherit, immediate semaphore
decrement, mutex-holder publication, priority inheritance before blocking,
and source-linked disinheritance after timeout. Active assertion paths call the stock port
seam, write zero through `0xFFFFFFFF`, and stop. The current-task getter is
the reviewed eight-byte stock seam at `0x0045589C`; the retained private queue
seams are generic create and mutex initialization, copy-to-queue, unlock, and
empty/full predicates. The post-timeout priority helper is now an appended
upstream-derived source leaf. Retained
task/list/port seams cover timeout, scheduler suspension/resumption, event
lists, mutex priority operations, critical sections, and yielding. Keeping
those seams explicit preserves the stock private ABI and defines the next
source-replacement boundary.

`runtime_freertos_queue.c` has SHA-256
`d54c7970600fd7719a9e847f431512bcc8e45ed942413621de7e93385f2376e0`.
Its production create, generic-send, recursive-give, and recursive-take bodies
occupy overlay offsets 105,948, 105,980, 106,572, and 106,648, with sizes 30,
556, 74, and 76 bytes. Their SHA-256 values are
`144a697bc812f31a14334b555deedfbcf4cbb2ed050413decd63da056966e5ed`,
`0cfc04164a987cbfd9a771640028db0f19d7480f0b76197600e109c51a5acc20`,
`9b01cee0779e203d578aaacee0f851c1930eb5e2dad68d4a06f63ce81497e745`,
and
`6ef349e5275d24710b29690b5b0040abd46acb779acc61730631bd1c365fa3f2`.
The legacy broad semaphore body is host-oracle-only. Production instead
appends the authenticated upstream candidate at offset 120,728 (602 linked
bytes, SHA-256
`77c3f659ca8916cd23c44f37e021f7a2c7f6bf9bf460b3f509cbebcc14e7193d`)
after its 18-byte helper at offset 120,708 (SHA-256
`fdb52b44dbd26f4b66e98b7e7586ad503c2dbb5c7e01ff5c9818b3536c2d2519`).
The candidate's only relocation is `R_ARM_THM_CALL` at relative offset 580 to
that helper. All five stock public bodies remain replaced with four-byte
`B.W` redirects and Thumb NOP fill. Recursive give has its source relocation;
recursive take instead materializes odd address `0x00441C45` into `r2` and
uses the one authenticated `BLX r2`, so it necessarily traverses the public
patch. Whole-image wide/narrow branch and byte-granular pointer scans find no
remaining route into the stock helper `[0x00441EC4,0x00441ED8)`, whose exact
official bytes remain unmodified. Seventeen
focused tests cover exact stock hashes and callers, target
ABI/symbols/seams, mutex creation, recursive ownership and count behavior,
real queue copy modes, binary and mutex give/take behavior, full/no-wait
failure, blocking retries, timeout races, waiter wakeups, yield decisions,
priority inheritance/disinheritance, and every public assertion gate.

The promotion changes the canonical Apple component by +32 bytes: 28 bytes
move into semantic `source_compiled` coverage and four bytes are explicit
alignment; opaque bytes do not change. Final Apple pins are overlay 121,330 /
`b0e7ec99bdf68b0b42b79e2bb935274f6b5a12d53a449cca3f021fa906ad1e3c`,
component 3,644,726 /
`d9af47dd5b4668f23722a530df40b12dfb926ef5c0cc6fb603733b2e14a05a17`,
and package 4,423,180 /
`74278f0c7ae44e5364a6bca3abc762fcb48a0b2dcb06d816412566c5e974541d`.
Exact-root Linux pins are overlay 123,184 /
`2ece296109ba518aa5e9474bc46dc0f77003abd57231c5becd6525dd18673c63`,
component 3,646,580 /
`0c65b98e4867b7aa143572ccb831879c88ebeded4c8e41d2e294a72bd0ea61a9`,
and package 4,425,034 /

### TLSF v3.1 source integration

#### Vendor provenance and recovered stock closure

The integrated allocator uses byte-identical `tlsf.c` and `tlsf.h` files from
Matthew Conte TLSF v3.1 candidate commit
`deff9ab509341f264addbd3c8ada533678591905`. Their SHA-256 values are
respectively
`2a0f8cfc9cfe6114ccdc6cf22339059440b16f1149b5107bead4ae4c3a0d50e2`
and
`f7f73c48810ba60203095667c226e5a600a6ea0f69afba48efff6efbaa628d4f`.
The binary cannot distinguish the exact upstream commit. The defensible
source-equivalent bound therefore remains
`a1f743ffac0305408b39e791e0ffb45f6d9bc777` through the selected
`deff9ab509341f264addbd3c8ada533678591905`; this range includes the observed
large-allocation bounds fix and ends at a signed-to-unsigned bitmap-literal
change that is instruction-equivalent for valid shifts. The stock IAR path
and assertion-line sequence independently identify
`third_party\tlsf\tlsf.c` and agree with this bounded state.

The official `s200_v2.2.6.10` TLSF code-and-literal closure is the half-open
span `0x004CFD18...0x004D09B4`, or inclusive
`0x004CFD18...0x004D09B3`. Its 3,228 bytes have SHA-256
`007d8ac1f0e118281a07f6bde1049256800894d9684dff16e1d316f1ea4a7f9d`.
The six reviewed literal islands are
`0x004D0604...0x004D0607`,
`0x004D06AC...0x004D06B3`,
`0x004D06D6...0x004D06EB`,
`0x004D0802...0x004D0807`,
`0x004D0852...0x004D0867`, and
`0x004D094A...0x004D09B3`.

Every externally reached stock body is independently hash-gated before its
non-linking `B.W` redirect and NOP fill are emitted:

| `0x004D0580...0x004D05E3` | 100 | `387065af5f49439c736ae479d48bb51da18413863c4fad7c06fd5e013d2d8e4a` | `open_cfw_tlsf_walk_pool` |

#### Complete caller closure

An exhaustive scan of every halfword-aligned Thumb-2 wide branch in the
complete official Apollo image finds 157 direct branches into the retained
TLSF closure: 133 internal and 24 external. All 157 are `BL`; none is
`B.W`. The complete source-sorted canonical branch record set has SHA-256
`0df083115ba1b63547b05e494985fe24e6d6a7e70aa4f887e5e7b47312e6e1db`.
The external distribution is:

| Stock entry | External call sites | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| `0x004D0580` | `0x0057F596` | 1 |
| `0x004D05E4` | `0x004841AE`, `0x0048420A`, `0x00484250`, `0x00484272`, `0x004842B8` | 5 |
| `0x004D05FA` | `0x0057F5AA` | 1 |
| `0x004D06EC` | `0x00484148`, `0x005EDA7C` | 2 |
| `0x004D0716` | `0x0057F56C` | 1 |
| `0x004D0722` | `0x00474CEE`, `0x004841A2`, `0x0057FAEC`, `0x0057FB1C`, `0x0057FE44` | 5 |
| `0x004D0744` | `0x004841FE` | 1 |
| `0x004D0808` | `0x00474D30`, `0x004842C2`, `0x0057FB48`, `0x0057FC08`, `0x0057FC1A`, `0x0057FED6` | 6 |
| `0x004D0868` | `0x00474D74`, `0x0048425C` | 2 |

For reproducibility, canonical records use lower-case
`source,target,kind,instruction-bytes` lines sorted by source. The 24 external
records have SHA-256
`722e5abdbf52daf7cbe038bd03332c3853fa6dd48e1f1eed9bce104c33e9d97b`;
their packed little-endian source-address list has SHA-256
`19c57946436a2fd587bde1a4a7ed4b1db2f7187d636818ae80e70b8475374ddb`;
and their packed little-endian `(source,target)` list has SHA-256
`dbb0ab6332aaaf1cb32fd6f830e57159989aff396d95bfdbbc7ea3b80d8d53bb`.
The 133 internal records have canonical SHA-256
`ed9b0361d0ce6e117349da99ffdf969818a10648f91cb1f9fbc1a2cc6de313f0`.

Capstone validation of each external containing function confirms that all 24
sites are live instructions and that all nine destinations are function
starts. No external branch lands in a function interior or literal island.
An all-byte-window stored-word scan finds no genuine external TLSF function
pointer; all 21 raw external numeric matches are UTF-16, coefficient-table,
or other packed-data false positives. The only genuine stored pointer is
internal literal `0x004D0994 = 0x004D0555`, the Thumb pointer to source role
`default_walker` at `0x004D0554`. No external `MOVW`/`MOVT` construction
resolves into the closure. Thus the nine redirected entries cover every
external direct or stored-pointer use of the stock allocator.

The closure has 27 outbound assertion/diagnostic calls to exactly
`0x004D09B4`, the first byte outside the half-open span. The source port does
not retain that opaque fatal-handler dependency: its assertion seam reports
through the reviewed ARM logger boundary and then traps locally.

#### Source port, ABI, seams, and integration topology

`runtime_tlsf.c` has SHA-256
`ca6eedb79a8975474b9e158179786c3e0bb958afade130ecf8e276b5555f1ca2`.
It is compiled immediately before the byte-preserved vendor source as a
freestanding prefix. Compile-time assertions require eight-bit bytes, ILP32
`int`, `long`, pointers, `size_t`, and `ptrdiff_t`, four-byte pointer
alignment, and the 32-bit unsigned range. The port deliberately undefines
Clang's GCC-compatibility macros before parsing TLSF so the reviewed generic
`ffs`/`fls` implementation is selected. The recovered G2 configuration is
four-byte allocation alignment, 32 second-level lists, 24 first-level lists,
a 128-byte small-block threshold, 16-byte free header, 12-byte minimum block,
four-byte allocation overhead, eight-byte pool overhead, maximum block size
`0x40000000`, `control_t` size `0xC74`, active assertions, and `_DEBUG`
disabled.

Six freestanding compatibility headers replace only the hosted C-library
surface: `assert.h`, `limits.h`, `stddef.h`, `stdio.h`, `stdlib.h`, and
`string.h`. Their SHA-256 values are respectively
`798db1564e14c14caa4b03b4c8efa874e96055cb49e238b5a4026a1d656924ef`,
`7df46c357072588c805781ea5cc2c6126348667e1e7ba377a1c3a2bcb5b648ca`,
`dfe4c45cb39bd92ed9a76623c78e6c9849627ad35139819c4c9d83fc90da410f`,
`0c4cfde236cb8aea29854aae71558ab2636824428ba48a4d295ce86cf7af345a`,
`51b0802d10419a971c531d2ffd4c7cf850d3a94d7d929827fa57147c7cc951c0`,
and
`26cfee2fb222dc2bb1d13ed631bc5a540f9d45b2ce96f48323a7cb5c92064938`.
The only port functions are the local assertion handler, diagnostic adapter,
and byte-copy implementation; there are no undefined target symbols.

The ARM diagnostic adapter preserves the reviewed firmware logger boundary:
it loads the dynamic handler from SRAM word `0x200742F0`, formats into context
`0x2006B930` through Thumb formatter entry `0x00473037`, reloads the handler,
and dispatches that context. A null handler suppresses logging. Assertion
failure logs once and then loops locally; it does not return with damaged
allocator metadata. The wasm32 proof lane intentionally uses a deterministic
no-op diagnostic because it has no firmware logger environment.

The integrated translation unit exports the complete 20-function TLSF public
API under the `open_cfw_tlsf_*` namespace, the three port functions, and seven
required local helpers: `default_walker`, `block_insert`,
`block_locate_free`, `block_merge_next`, `block_prepare_used`,
`block_remove`, and `block_split`. These are the final 30 entries in the
515-function overlay topology. Exactly nine stock patch sites redirect the
externally reached public functions listed above; source-to-source calls and
all allocator internals resolve within the overlay. The original 3,228-byte
closure remains physically partitioned as compatibility data/code, but its
complete external entry closure is redirected to source.

The target build is ELF32 little-endian ARM (`e_machine = 40`) and the source
enforces the Apollo510 ILP32 ABI. A separate wasm32-ILP32 execution oracle
compiles, links without imports, allocates 256 KiB of memory, and returns
zero after allocator create, allocate, align, resize, coalesce, walk, and
integrity checks. Its current object is 145,930 bytes with SHA-256
`e150362cd78aa23e5399515540106ab000bd870e02054225e3b5cb4707a56000`;
the stripped module is 9,018 bytes with SHA-256
`198e6d5bae33d502605ac1696f764a4bd0cf1c7653433315c79afa862228c3eb`.
The ordinary native host lane exercises allocator semantics and deterministic
stress, but on a 64-bit host it is explicitly semantic coverage only and is
not proof of the target's 32-bit ABI. The ELF32 ARM build and wasm32-ILP32
oracle provide the independent ABI-sized evidence.

### Variadic formatter core and public wrappers

The public `snprintf` wrapper occupies stock
`0x00483FD0...0x00483FE9` (26 bytes, SHA-256
`a7bbf413eb4e6661219f9fa0f0b2e90ec4ff1f6321af913ea5b0561c19700bbe`);
the public `vsnprintf` wrapper occupies
`0x00483FEA...0x00483FFB` (18 bytes, SHA-256
`efd2fb98268737ddd968133f20a0ae190b499fb11e24abeab8bfd69a239b388f`).
The reviewed mpaland-derived dispatcher/core occupies
`0x00483960...0x00483FCB` (1,644 bytes, SHA-256
`69f04620a01aaca4a11601ea426644fa3e2bd47c972700c6ddc1676607e1435b`).
Its only stock entries are the self-recursive call at `0x00483D3E` and the
two public-wrapper calls at `0x00483FE0` and `0x00483FF6`; exhaustive wide,
narrow, and stored-pointer scans find no alternate external interior entry.
The following aligned word
`0x00483FCC...0x00483FCF` is the reversed `fni-\0` token formerly read by
stock `ftoa` at `0x0048339A`; it is not core data and is inactive because the
fixed-format converter is already source-owned.

`runtime_vsnprintf.c` has SHA-256
`3229a2c14011a3025962d2b2477f73c92bf93acbaee7d304e78e7b883f6c31de`.
It implements the complete integer, pointer, float, exponential/general,
character, string, percent, unknown-specifier, flag, width, precision, and
length-modifier paths. It preserves the reviewed 32-bit AAPCS argument cursor,
8-byte alignment for `long long` and `double`, unsigned `%hhd`, attempted
length and final-termination behavior, null-buffer no-op callback, G2
hash-prefixed pointer policy, and both recursive `%PV` and `%pV` descriptor
forms. Recursion deliberately preserves stock's unsigned
`maximum_length - index` underflow and emits both nested and outer
terminators. Malformed trailing-percent behavior remains a documented
stock-compatible out-of-domain quirk.

The linked core is 1,550 bytes at overlay offset 99,000 (SHA-256
`1aa6f6875a5d29ee8a71eeba8757bc88fe6bdbdb818e528c64d6541fbe82ab51`).
Its ten callable dependencies resolve directly to the already source-owned
digit, decimal-parser, integer, floating, and bounded-string functions; its
recursive call also resolves to itself. No compiler `__aeabi` floating helper
is introduced.

`runtime_printf_wrappers.c` has SHA-256
`c28318100a6eb00d476df9253cbf2d28c202c78f27d1529f2fcd826a355f7971`.
The linked `snprintf` body is 52 bytes at overlay offset 100,660 (SHA-256
`5e07793da9d3dbacb2993b1c5d8311a7ebf0358843ac25e7ef9cb52bdb1ac7d7`);
the linked `vsnprintf` body is 34 bytes at offset 100,712 (SHA-256
`2ea9aa4d62e52065ea58057df17fbe9c6041db003cb402e6b58bf17b429e8bf3`).
Both wrappers now call the source core directly. The core and wrapper suites
contribute 25 focused behavioral, ABI, topology, boundary, and target-artifact
tests.

### LVGL asynchronous call lifecycle

The asynchronous-call creator occupies stock
`0x00484014...0x00484051` (62 bytes, SHA-256
`4a3b8927b10dd11d3b872207c2138dd85494060f948727dc021025c3b57c174f`);
cancellation occupies
`0x00484052...0x004840A9` (88 bytes, SHA-256
`67cd3979de3365531652c6de47f55bbab9541e753c5091a8423229635ce99900`);
and the timer callback occupies
`0x004840AC...0x004840C5` (26 bytes, SHA-256
`39c550823fd1d0bb1b80f29119c66bd33d2751de30c9d4c2ccc987bd99e5c8d8`).
Callback identity remains the legacy Thumb value `0x004840AD`, so timer
creation and cancellation compare the same stored callback pointer.

`runtime_async_call.c` has SHA-256
`9863d3da2e18d6c62694d3a33bc0d84b4384525d631f97bde823612e4fbb19cb`.
It uses reviewed fixed Thumb seams for allocation (`0x0044F719`), free
(`0x0044F759`), timer creation (`0x00464467`), repeat count
(`0x004645AD`), deletion (`0x004644EF`), and next-timer traversal
(`0x004645ED`). Cancellation saves the next node before deletion, removes
every exact callback/user-data match, and deletes before freeing. The timer
callback saves user state before deleting/freeing the timer and invokes the
saved callback last.

The linked creator is 88 bytes at overlay offset 101,232 (SHA-256
`d887df3e763e412124b02615e3785dda2da71db7bd9b696d369126045874a74b`);
cancellation is 116 bytes at offset 101,320 (SHA-256
`5fc6f6009d551fef6cd4c5490a8e09d816e4d98b22e70a88430d2f2ef54e8c1a`);
and the callback is 40 bytes at offset 101,436 (SHA-256
`6e9464c3aad06063d0642d5b54af01cdb356b94ab314e4094087f80f6f524ec6`).
Twelve focused tests cover allocation/timer failures, success, callback
ordering and reentrancy, empty and duplicate cancellation, exact matching,
stock topology, dependency seams, and relocation-free target code.

The authenticated FreeRTOS-Kernel V10.5.1 snapshot under
`third_party/freertos-kernel` contains 48 pristine upstream files
(1,455,419 bytes): all seven core implementation units, all 19 released
headers, `portable/Common/mpu_wrappers.c`, and both complete released IAR
Cortex-M55 port alternatives. Official annotated tag object
`d7b40dbed508c305c2a32ccf3982045ec9ba8734` peels to commit
`def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c` and tree
`7496dfa815c3cea2f45a090c6e92d113f494b930`. The tag is not
cryptographically signed, so the provenance boundary explicitly pins the
official repository, tag, commit, tree, and every file by byte count, Git
blob SHA-1, and SHA-256. The snapshot deliberately does not select
`ARM_CM55` versus `ARM_CM55_NTZ`; G2 TrustZone, interrupt, tick, FPU/MVE,
hook, allocator, and `FreeRTOSConfig.h` settings require focused evidence
before either port may be linked.

The littlefs port audit recovers the standard v2.10.1 callback ABI, the
external mapping `0x01400000 + block * 0x1000 + offset`, the
`0x01400000...0x01FC0000` partition, and the driver result mapping from zero
to success and nonzero to `LFS_ERR_IO` (`-5`). It also identifies the
Apollo-main read/program/erase seams at `0x00471021`, `0x004708A9`, and
`0x0047075D`, and the bootloader equivalents at `0x00420F71`,
`0x00420B0D`, and `0x00420A09`. A bounded `LFS_READONLY` port is feasible,
but no redirect is installed without a golden external-flash capture; all
format/program/erase paths remain prohibited.

The first FreeRTOS queue-private increment source-owns `prvIsQueueEmpty` at
`[0x00441FF6,0x00442012)` and `prvIsQueueFull` at
`[0x00442012,0x00442030)`. The 28- and 30-byte stock bodies have SHA-256
`fb24b5bf27e2d16d89d87554fc4c93fdc8b94cd42bd72613b9e28336ef23932e`
and
`bd4e5d3f3b08830ccc68d8f7e8f7b4fe930d111a7785ba40784ac2bfb0c73faf`.
All five external calls target an entry, no external control transfer or
stored pointer targets an interior instruction, and the five public queue
operations remain source-owned. Generic send and semaphore/mutex take now
call the predicates directly as source-to-source dependencies; recursive
give/take reach them through those public operations, while mutex creation

recovered all three callers, its sole SPOT-manager dependency, the absence of
executable alternate entries, and nine byte-unaligned accidental interior
values that are explicitly retained as negative evidence.
`DumpContainingFunctions.java 0x00480058` bounded and decompiled the
following system-PLL enable routine; indexed and raw scans recovered its two
callers, interrupt/delay dependencies, three register literals, next function
at `0x0048009E`, absence of executable alternate entries, and two byte-wise
interior-value false positives crossing 16-bit data-table fields.

`DumpFunctionRange.java 0x00480312 0x00480434`,

and the `0x00480434` next boundary. Exhaustive raw `BL`/`B.W` and aligned
stored-pointer scans independently checked all 13 spans and separated eight

The MCUCTRL information-getter pass used the existing Ghidra 12.1.2 function
at `0x00480D72`, its two indexed executable references, and containing-

halfword-aligned `BL`/`B.W`, external-interior-target, and aligned stored-
Thumb-pointer scans confirmed the 250-byte body, both source-owned helper

## Final FreeRTOS task and littlefs leaf integration

The final upstream-first increment adds seven Apollo-main functions without
re-creating either library:

| Upstream function | Stock span | Overlay offset | Target bytes |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| FreeRTOS V10.5.1 `xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandle` | `[0x0045589C,0x004558A4)` | 108,980 | 12 |
| littlefs v2.10.1 `lfs_alloc_drop` | `[0x004CB0E6,0x004CB0F6)` | 108,992 | 12 |
| FreeRTOS V10.5.1 `uxTaskGetNumberOfTasks` | `[0x00454F10,0x00454F16)` | 109,004 | 12 |
| FreeRTOS V10.5.1 `xTaskGetSchedulerState` | `[0x004558A4,0x004558C4)` | 109,016 | 32 |
| littlefs v2.10.1 `lfs_fs_disk_version` | `[0x004CB0C4,0x004CB0CA)` | 109,048 | 8 |
| littlefs v2.10.1 `lfs_mlist_append` | `[0x004CB0BC,0x004CB0C4)` | 109,056 | 8 |
| littlefs v2.10.1 `lfs_mlist_remove` | `[0x004CB0A0,0x004CB0BC)` | 109,064 | 56 |

Focused disassembly is limited to the configuration and ABI facts that
upstream source cannot supply. For the task getters, it pins
`pxCurrentTCB`-equivalent storage at `0x20074A20`, the current task count at
`0x20074A30`, and scheduler state at `0x20074A3C` and `0x20074A58`. For
littlefs it distinguishes the Apollo-main `-O2` code-generation profile from
the bootloader `-Oz` profile and confirms the private list-node layout. No
unidentified library behavior is substituted into these seven bodies.

Together with the earlier `lfs_scmp`, `lfs_alloc_ckpoint`, and
`lfs_file_tell_` integrations, Apollo main now source-owns seven littlefs
v2.10.1 leaves. The raw bootloader provider source-owns the six copies present
there: `lfs_scmp` at `[0x004104BA,0x004104BE)`, `lfs_mlist_remove` at
`[0x00410DA8,0x00410DC4)`, `lfs_mlist_append` at
`[0x00410DC4,0x00410DCC)`, `lfs_fs_disk_version` at
`[0x00410DCC,0x00410DD2)`, `lfs_alloc_ckpoint` at
`[0x00410DE8,0x00410DEE)`, and `lfs_alloc_drop` at
`[0x00410DEE,0x00410DFE)`. Its 58-byte overlay at
`[0x00434478,0x004344B2)` has SHA-256
`77a8601995931d5ca7dad2f1ff90100b6f8e6cb88cf248198142498f588a5e65`.
The resulting 148,658-byte provider has SHA-256
`b55f3619d135aef87b1cea1b8c1128b067c189b89bc74ea1811c2523a33fa560`,
15,182 bytes of remaining bootloader headroom, and regenerated outer CRC-32C
`0xE7D39054`.

The final Apollo-main link places the two delayed TLSF helpers immediately
after these leaves: `block_split` at offset 109,120 for 184 bytes and
`block_remove` at offset 109,304 for 220 bytes. Linked text ends at offset
109,524, followed by four alignment bytes and 4,000 bytes of read-only-data
accounting. The complete overlay is 113,524 bytes at
`[0x00794324,0x007AFE98)` with SHA-256
`d84ab2b9e0e00956d2094139f4ac65d09766f3efcf5fbe6144f5f41fb5c7a8b8`.
It contains 548 compiled functions, 518 hash-validated replacement sites, and
902 resolved relocations from 291 pinned source inputs.

The complete 3,636,920-byte Apollo component has SHA-256
`be7d6587bc7b3c1bc3ff2350a64fb9595f49027e0c2dac0e72d8044f513ea38a`.
Its 3,636,888 installed bytes leave 262,504 bytes below `0x007F0000` and

`976f886215798140672857f969f1ff434dfdf98d9fd13d38a94f2ad1021297ad`
and a flash plan with 693 placed regions and two deliberately unresolved

The seven integration suites pass 55 focused upstream-oracle, ABI,
stock-span, target-body, manifest, and source-hash tests. The final
bootloader overlay passes ten focused provider, redirect, CRC, ownership, and
mutation-boundary tests. A complete 243-test Apollo-main aggregate run first
surfaced 16 relocation-sensitive expected-hash failures after the appended
functions moved later code and data; it produced no semantic behavior
failure. Each changed body and relocation inventory was reviewed and
repinned, and all ten affected aggregate methods then passed on rerun. The
subsequent whole-repository release gate passes all 1,706 tests in 828.498
seconds.

Three final output-isolated lanes under
`build/repro-final-upstream-{a,b,c}` independently produce identical
113,524-byte Apollo-main overlays, 3,636,920-byte Apollo-main providers,
58-byte bootloader overlays, 148,658-byte bootloader providers, and
4,414,810-byte EVENOTA packages with the hashes pinned above. The EVENOTA
analyzer accepts final topology, layout, and every checksum. Both the
direct-temple and case-bridge offline inspectors accept the main-only transfer
plan as 3,637 records covering 3,636,888 installed bytes through
`0x007AFE98`; bootloader and peripheral transfer remain policy-rejected.
These were offline operations: this section does not claim physical
installation or hardware behavior.

## FreeRTOS queue-creation source integration

The next upstream-first increment source-owns the complete contiguous
FreeRTOS-Kernel V10.5.1 queue-creation cluster rather than re-creating it
from decompilation:

| Released function | Official stock span | Stock bytes | Overlay function |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `xQueueGenericCreateStatic` | `[0x004415CA,0x00441636)` | 108 | `open_cfw_freertos_queue_generic_create_static` |
| `xQueueGenericCreate` | `[0x00441636,0x00441696)` | 96 | `open_cfw_freertos_queue_generic_create` |
| `prvInitialiseNewQueue` | `[0x00441696,0x004416B8)` | 34 | `open_cfw_freertos_queue_initialise_new` |
| `prvInitialiseMutex` | `[0x004416B8,0x004416D6)` | 30 | `open_cfw_freertos_queue_initialise_mutex` |

The 268-byte stock cluster has SHA-256
`88026bc2cb8b45e5983a6e34072ff2be0767a06775930305310dfcdf28bd48ad`.
Whole-image scans find 5, 6, 2, and 2 direct callers, respectively, with no
external interior branch, narrow branch, `B.W`, or aligned stored entry or
interior reference. All four complete entries are therefore redirected using
the existing `B.W` plus NOP-fill policy.

The implementation is a bounded, MIT-retaining port of authenticated
FreeRTOS commit `def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c`. Focused
disassembly supplies the G2-specific configuration that pristine source alone
cannot select: `Queue_t` is 80 bytes, both static and dynamic allocation are
enabled, mutexes and trace fields are enabled, queue sets are disabled, the
allocation marker is at `+0x46`, and the queue-type byte is at `+0x4C`.
Trace creation hooks are empty. The source retains explicit reviewed seams to
`xQueueGenericReset` at `0x00441516`, the V10.5.1 `heap_4` allocator at
`0x00456110`, and the assertion/port trap at `0x005FA0A4`. The mutex
initializer calls the already source-owned generic-send implementation.

The new source unit compiles to 344 linked text bytes:

| Overlay offset | Bytes | Function |
|---:|---:|---|
| 109,120 | 130 | static generic creator |
| 109,252 | 38 | new-queue initializer |
| 109,292 | 138 | dynamic generic creator |
| 109,432 | 32 | mutex initializer |

Six compiler-alignment bytes separate the four functions. The delayed TLSF
helpers now begin at offsets 109,464 and 109,648. Linked text closes at
109,868, followed by four alignment bytes and the unchanged 4,000 bytes of
read-only-data accounting.

The current Apollo-main overlay is 113,868 bytes at
`[0x00794324,0x007AFFF0)` with SHA-256
`0d485ef1ddf9766169689dc21bb85e5864243e2daa8c0b63263a281aeb295b50`.
It contains 552 compiled functions, 522 replacement sites covering 79,606
stock bytes, and 905 resolved relocations from 292 pinned primary source
inputs. The complete 3,637,264-byte Apollo component has SHA-256
`124664d6cd9673dabf460865ecf01b85f93ca6271b3e75ceecc4cd608d271a09`;
its 3,637,232 installed bytes leave 262,160 bytes below `0x007F0000` and
319,504 bytes below `0x007FE000`.

The 4,415,154-byte EVENOTA package has SHA-256
`68913e18f581fbb16fc071e4f49015bf9bf494cfd81d06e296c8eaf167f23e7f`
and 697 placed flash regions plus the same two deliberately unresolved
controller regions. Package ownership is 114,057 source-compiled bytes
(2.580340%), 80,651 other generated bytes (1.826686%), and 4,220,577 opaque
bytes (95.592974%).

The preceding “Final FreeRTOS task and littlefs leaf integration” section is
retained as the reproducibility record for the immediately prior milestone.
It no longer describes the current release artifact.

The completed release gate passes all 244 Apollo-main aggregate tests in
526.769 seconds and all 1,763 repository tests in 873.770 seconds. The
manifest verifier authenticates all six providers and reproduces the package
SHA-256 above; the littlefs, FreeRTOS, AmbiqSuite, CMSIS, TLSF, and EasyLogger
snapshot verifiers and the read-only upstream analyzers all pass. Three
independent output trees under `build/repro-queue-create-{a,b,c}` reproduce
byte-identical bootloader providers, Apollo-main overlays, Apollo-main
providers, EVENOTA packages, and flash plans. Their respective SHA-256 values

`0494ce7169f06a734a7bd7585f49a9fa91fa7318`. The explicit fallback

### `in_place_leaves` safety contract

The five names are not members of the appended overlay `functions` ABI and
are not `patch_sites` targets. For each record the builder:

1. authenticates the common source and reviewed compiler family and flags;
2. compiles one fixed-address leaf while discarding the other allocated
   sections;
3. requires exact stock and expected size/SHA-256 pins;
4. rejects any relocation not present in the ordered six-record allowlist;
5. resolves PC-relative literals and Thumb branches only at the declared
   stock runtime address;
6. authenticates each referenced four-byte literal in the base image;
7. rejects overlap between source bodies, their protected literal words, the
   appended overlay, or any other declared write; and
8. compares the original stock span before installing the exact compiled
   result.

This contract preserves vector addresses, exception latency, frame ordering,
the conditional floating-point high-register save/restore, `BASEPRI=0x30`,
and the released DSB/ISB ordering. It also reports fixed-address source
ownership separately from appended overlay ownership.

## Prior CMSIS-FreeRTOS `osMessageQueueNew` source tranche

That build compiled the exact CMSIS-FreeRTOS v10.5.1
`osMessageQueueNew` allocation and validation algorithm from the 8,427-byte
`runtime_cmsis_message_queue_new.c`, SHA-256
`8897019aa7a2beca32a88dc60808fb1f99b1538933b8ab4fbd9ed4fed38d433c`.
It is pinned to authenticated `cmsis_os2.c` at commit
`d213f261b5be6bb29a7cce8b84071706b72f4d53`, whose complete 70,106-byte
file has SHA-256
`8a0d60b56ad30c4f7957f64fa581158017b6812ec94b832d974c773ae4f2bc36`.
The bounded adapter retains Arm's Apache-2.0 copyright and SPDX terms; the
three separately reached FreeRTOS V10.5.1 functions retain MIT terms.

Focused disassembly establishes the selected G2 seams: static and dynamic
allocation are enabled, `configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE` is zero,
`StaticQueue_t` is 80 bytes, and the 32-bit `osMessageQueueAttr_t` is 24
bytes with `name/attr_bits/cb_mem/cb_size/mq_mem/mq_size` at offsets
`0x00/0x04/0x08/0x0C/0x10/0x14`. The inlined `IRQ_Context` rejects handler
mode immediately; after the scheduler starts it also rejects masked thread
mode when either `PRIMASK` or `BASEPRI` is nonzero. Static creation requires
both buffers and sufficient sizes, all-zero attributes select dynamic
creation, and mixed attributes or zero dimensions return null.

70,106-byte upstream file has SHA-256
`8a0d60b56ad30c4f7957f64fa581158017b6812ec94b832d974c773ae4f2bc36`.
The bounded adapter retains Arm's Apache-2.0 terms. The separately reached
FreeRTOS-Kernel V10.5.1 scheduler-state and mutex-creator dependencies are
pinned to commit `def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c` and retain
MIT terms.

The exact V10.5.1 `portable/MemMang/heap_4.c` is now retained by the
49-file FreeRTOS snapshot as an authenticated, unselected reference. Its

`d48a51e34caed771e6650d95f6c2527e52fde2a6ebc6f83b49d003aef0135e05`
and upstream Git blob `3af0caf2b60fc4adfb103a115fefbf1b09b21dd8`. It remains

production closure.

### Recovered G2 configuration and ABI

Focused disassembly selects:

- `configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION=1`;
- `configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION=1`;
- `configUSE_RECURSIVE_MUTEXES=1`;
- `configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE=0`;
- `osMutexRecursive=0x1`, with the low bit set on a successful recursive
  handle;
- `osMutexPrioInherit=0x2`, with no separate constructor branch;
- `osMutexRobust=0x8`, which is rejected;
- an 80-byte `StaticSemaphore_t`; and
- a 16-byte 32-bit `osMutexAttr_t`, with
  `name/attr_bits/cb_mem/cb_size` at `+0x00/+0x04/+0x08/+0x0C`.

Null attributes and a zeroed attribute record select dynamic ordinary-mutex
creation. Static creation requires a non-null control block of at least 80
bytes. Mixed control-block fields and robust mutexes return null. The inlined
recovered `IRQ_Context` policy reads `IPSR` first, rejects handler mode
immediately, and after scheduler start rejects masked thread mode when either
`PRIMASK` or `BASEPRI` is nonzero.

### Authenticated source, configuration, and license boundary

Apollo main now source-owns both FreeRTOS tick-query entries and their
shared volatile-word provider. The admitted files are:

|---|---:|---|
| `components/shared/freertos/runtime_freertos_tick_count.c` | 3,412 | `948d1b2de6026adc7cf84a34a359c859c32126b3afcafe92c2347f5f7ab56363` |
| `components/shared/freertos/runtime_freertos_tick_count.h` | 1,186 | `adc4065b3504a7eacb2e29e2d357636917e2b690afc49b265689e36d66171dae` |

The implementation is a bounded adaptation of `xTaskGetTickCount` and
`xTaskGetTickCountFromISR` from the authenticated FreeRTOS-Kernel V10.5.1
`tasks.c` at commit
`def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c` and tree
`7496dfa815c3cea2f45a090c6e92d113f494b930`. The complete 223,695-byte
`tasks.c` has SHA-256
`14020d617b96dd2814e1211f6e3b645bcf5e2bd3179c23fe7dd16bc666fe9463`.
The 49-file vendored snapshot verifier authenticates the official unsigned
annotated tag, peeled commit, tree, selected Git blobs, SHA-256 values, and
1,036-byte MIT license, whose SHA-256 is
`508a77d2e7b51d98adeed32648ad124b7b30241a8e70b2e72c99f92d8e5874d1`.
Copyright (C) 2021 Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. The complete MIT terms
remain in the shared source, `third_party/freertos-kernel/LICENSE.md`, and
`LICENSE-FreeRTOS-MIT`.

The reviewed official input remains the 3,523,396-byte
`blobs/official/g2-2.2.6.10/ota_s200_firmware_ota.bin`, SHA-256
`36c5b0e499a68ac2493a497bdab9740fd3e7027730c26a9094eca47268a27863`.
Removing its 32-byte preamble yields the authenticated 3,523,364-byte
installed application, SHA-256
`19044a72bdfeb04c6b1b104d87da7b98e13cc18928528d84d999b6bcc0ba9701`.

Focused configuration evidence selects 32-bit `TickType_t`,
`configUSE_16_BIT_TICKS=0`, and the IAR Cortex-M55 NTZ port's
`portTICK_TYPE_IS_ATOMIC=1`. The released normal critical-section macros
therefore compile away, while the ISR mask-acquire macro becomes constant
zero and its clear macro becomes a no-op. The official ISR body's leading
`movs r0,#0` is the retained saved-mask assignment, not an alternate entry
or extra state read. This boundary does not claim a complete historical G2
`FreeRTOSConfig.h`; the official 32-bit loads independently establish the
tick-width and atomic-read behavior required by these two functions.

The exact pair bytes are

`xTaskGetTickCount` has exactly nine direct `BL` callers:

`ebb370ca83af193212df4dcbadcc5d87bc0de2f0` as the maintained
decompression source. The selected closure contains only
`LZ4_decompress_safe`, 64 bytes of `inc32table`/`dec64table` read-only data,
the four-byte G2 ABI tail adapter, and the 30-byte EvenHub mode-2 adapter. It
contains no compressor, frame API, writable section, or other public LZ4
entry. This production selection does not assert that the stock image is the
same point release.

The relocated placements and exact section pins are:

| Region | Apple clang 21 | Linux clang 22.1.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Decoder text | `[0x007B0B74,0x007B11F0)`, 1,660 bytes, `a7e5690af5e74e5395a51a716c9ebde2ee692dcf38decbf92141a3be261d358e` | `[0x007B12A8,0x007B1942)`, 1,690 bytes, `632ad34cdf299a714e4d81b7f2ba55e4edb1ac897ff65744622ab29b914bc542` |
| Alignment before tables | none | `[0x007B1942,0x007B1944)`, two generated zero bytes |
| `inc32table` + `dec64table` | `[0x007B11F0,0x007B1230)`, 64 bytes, `361b3c2a85717050294fd9e3c6440690de35c0a9455d50e487ea8f0881c40f03` | `[0x007B1944,0x007B1984)`, same 64 bytes and hash |
| Safe ABI adapter | `[0x007B1230,0x007B1234)`, four bytes, `589f67fc5b672f2be0809e999e8168708b11b90452088fb401a8d76d604959f5` | `[0x007B1984,0x007B1988)`, four bytes, `b30709dd4480368a7662bc4ec880846e7d74cb1da1386d4bbad8240d447894c2` |
| Mode-2 adapter | `[0x007B1234,0x007B1252)`, 30 bytes, `577501eac08ce8028c0262f19c84864439e11378314bc9f2874bd8acc77729b6` | `[0x007B1988,0x007B19A6)`, same size and hash |

The unrelocated decoder text hashes are
`3bb106d1a943c19f0c3f6e2252ae1fbb2bbb78a8a69772e4729a15596bc9da49`
for Apple and
`6d7e83dea96cf39e7ff5d65a1f66116ced40d3f952d2b2074913fd97fd0a916b`
for Linux. The relocated decoder-plus-table closures are respectively 1,724
bytes / `dc4a643ed862582b1cde268c894f74c51adabf9c242620179f5a6e4f3601cddf`
and 1,756 bytes / `499387fe05f3c3676375779ede3138e09efea4617efaf5b1a9ff68a3cd5efd62`.

The complete 40-byte stock mode-2 entry at `0x004E0C0C` redirects to the
active mode-2 leaf; the complete 30-byte stock safe entry at `0x0054F338`
redirects to the active safe adapter. The earlier primary-overlay mode-2 and
hand-decoder sections remain byte-stable under
`open_cfw_evenhub_mode2_decompress_legacy` and
`open_cfw_lz4_decompress_safe_legacy`. Apple retains them at
`[0x007973E8,0x00797406)` and `[0x00797408,0x007976C0)`; their sizes are 30
and 696 bytes. Linux retains the corresponding 30- and 650-byte sections at
its existing profile-specific primary positions. They are unreachable and
are retained solely to avoid shifting the established primary overlay.

The stock generic decoder `[0x0054EF08,0x0054F338)` and variable-length
reader `[0x0054EE90,0x0054EF08)` remain opaque compatibility bytes. The
official-image audit closes the live topology as three application callers to
mode-2, then safe, generic, and reader. Retargeting safe cuts the sole route to
generic and reader. Exhaustive Thumb branch decoding and a byte-granular scan
for even and Thumb pointers found no hidden entry or interior route. Exact
spans, hashes, false-positive classifications, and caller-set digests are in
`docs/research/lz4-stock-reachability-memory-provider-audit.md`.

The selected upstream object calls fixed stock EABI providers only:

| `__aeabi_memcpy` | `[0x00439BE4,0x00439C8A)`, 166 bytes | `8e696e1fb54917a436f850e562f74e8cc8734c259fdaac9f767a3c264ff427cd` | void EABI `(r0 destination, r1 source, r2 count)`; includes alternate entry `0x00439C04` |
| `__aeabi_memmove` | `[0x00439710,0x004397A6)`, 150 bytes | `31caf15ad676c4a99eace5673e1fe46b818b64d901707c461074e8acc5474b28` | same void EABI; complete backward-copy returns and non-linking non-overlap tail to `memcpy` audited |

The object does not consume a C-style returned destination pointer. These two
spans remain explicit opaque dependencies until source-owned EABI shims replace

## Preceding FreeRTOS `xTaskCheckForTimeOut` production integration

The current production profile appends a bounded adaptation of the exact
FreeRTOS-Kernel V10.5.1 `xTaskCheckForTimeOut` algorithm from authenticated
commit `def7d2df2b0506d3d249334974f51e427c17a41c`. The source boundary is:

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `components/shared/freertos/runtime_freertos_task_check_for_timeout.c` | 3,506 | `d0d84996ae7ab897cf53655962e86574577b98bf367df52c9ae8ac076a8dc89e` |
| `components/shared/freertos/runtime_freertos_task_check_for_timeout.h` | 5,152 | `a4704e71126df108833878ee3ddcf51a744f4b02cae9519a4d03fe308f0abcbc` |

The implementation retains the upstream MIT notice. The complete official
body is `[0x00455566,0x004555E6)`, 128 bytes with SHA-256
`83a983995a285b3257a1213bdbe3fa0542bae0c9296a88fd8b22c1388abdf72c`.
Exactly three direct calls reach its entry, at `0x004418C0`, `0x00441BCA`,
and `0x00441CF6`; no external branch or stored pointer reaches an interior
instruction. The function's five outgoing calls bind the two assertion
paths to `0x005FA0A4`, critical entry/exit to `0x004420D0` and
`0x004420E8`, and its partial-wait refresh to the already source-owned
`vTaskInternalSetTimeOutState` at `0x00455556`.

Focused disassembly proves the production selections
`INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend=1`, `INCLUDE_xTaskAbortDelay=0`, 32-bit unsigned ticks,
and `portMAX_DELAY=UINT32_MAX`. It also pins `xTickCount=0x20074A34`,
`xNumOfOverflows=0x20074A48`, and the eight-byte, four-aligned `TimeOut_t`
layout with signed overflow count at `+0` and unsigned entry tick at `+4`.
These G2-specific values are recovered parameters; the function algorithm
and license are upstream facts.

Both reviewed compilers emit one four-byte-aligned, relocation-free 136-byte
function section. Apple clang 21 emits SHA-256
`33f0782fa8af468bccf78b558cc010a9f7a89f30c7c76abced9a799feb6a93f5`
and places it at `[0x007B1440,0x007B14C8)`, after alignment
`[0x007B143E,0x007B1440)`. Homebrew clang 22.1.8 emits SHA-256
`486515dfdbdb1e175321445df167dca27357f270421b2d00492268e8da7c815c`
and places it at `[0x007B1B94,0x007B1C1C)`, after alignment
`[0x007B1B92,0x007B1B94)`. The compiler difference is instruction scheduling
(`LDR` pairs versus `LDRD`), not an ABI or semantic difference.

`[0x00448D4E,0x00448DD2)` to
`open_cfw_g2_easylogger_async_record_build_single_owner`. The stock entry,
132-byte expected hash, sole caller, and lack of exterior interior-entry
targets are unchanged. The selected source has SHA-256
`3b9588c36deb0d8dce58db71077530c86bb1f00f2ddeaca04f29e64946bf1b8f`.
